Page ii
Introduction
The following document is the specification of the REST API for Appointment management.
It includes the model definition as well as all available operations.
An
Appointment
is
an
arrangement
for
service
provider
personnel
to
carry
out
some
activity at a particular time and place, typically (but not exclusively) at customer premises.
It
could
be
used
to
install
a
product
service,
deliver
a
product
order
item
or
solve
a
customer problem.
An appointment is previously made during a customer interaction or self-service channel
and
has
two
phases
in
its
creation:
the
search
for
a
free
time
slot
based
on
given
parameters and the creation of the appointment with all the necessary information. After
this, the API gives the option to modify or delete the created appointment, as well, via the
event architecture, it is possible to notify any change in the appointment.

SAMPLE USE CASES
Use Case Id
UC_TMF_Appointment_001
Use Case Name
Create a New Appointment
Summary
A Customer uses a self-service channel to create a new appointment
to solve a problem with their internet service.
Actor(s)
1. Customer
2. Self-service channel
Pre-Conditions
1. The customer is already logged in the self-service channel
Begins When
All pre-conditions have been met and the customer access the
module to create and appointment for service support.
Description
1. The customer access the appointment module
2.
The
module
request
and
display
the
available
timeslots
for
the
customer
3. The customer select a proper timeslot
4.
The
customer
provide
all
the
information
required
for
the
appointment
such
as
contactMedium
for
the
contact
information,
relatedPlace
for
the
place
of
the
appointment,
relatedParty
for
the
person who is going to receive the appointment, among others.
5. The customer confirm the information and create the appointment.
6.
The
creation
of
the
appointment
triggers
a
notification
to
all
the
parts subscribed to the create appointment event.
Use Case Id
UC_TMF_Appointment_002
Use Case Name
Update an Appointment
Summary
A Customer calls the call center to modify an appointment
Actor(s)
1. Customer
2. Call center agent
Pre-Conditions
1. The customer already has an appointment to modify
Begins When
All pre-conditions have been met and the call center has access to the
customer data in the system

Use Case Id
UC_TMF_Appointment_003

Cancel an Appointment
Summary
A Customer calls the call center to cancel an appointment
Actor(s)
1. Customer
2. Call center agent
Pre-Conditions
1. The customer already has an appointment to modify
Begins When
All pre-conditions have been met and the call center has access to the
customer data in the system
Description
1. The customer provide all the information required for the call center
2. The call center agent look for all the appointments of this customer
3. The call center agent select the appointment that should be cancel
4.
The
call
center
agent
cancel
the
appointment
as
the
customer
required
5. The appointment is cancel and this triggers a notification to all the
parts subscribed to the cancel appointment event
Appointment Lifecycle States
This
Lifecycle
Management
is
responsible
for
managing
the
entire
lifecycle
of
the
Appointment.
An
appointment
progresses
through
a
series
of
states
from
creation
to
Appointment User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 3
completion. The state of an appointment indicates its current status and determines the
actions that can be performed.
Pending
: The appointment has been created but has not yet been Confirmed or Cancelled.
Confirmed
: The appointment has been accepted and scheduled to occur.
Rescheduled
:
The
appointment
has
been
moved
to
a
new
date
or
time.
A
rescheduled
appointment must be confirmed again before it can proceed.
In Progress
: The appointment is currently being executed.
Completed
: The appointment has been successfully fulfilled.
Failed
:
The
appointment
started
but
could
not
be
completed
successfully.
It
can
be
Rescheduled if needed.
Appointment User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 4
Cancelled
: The appointment has been terminated before execution.
Expired
: The appointment became invalid because the required action was not completed
within the allowed timeframe and it is now Cancelled.
Once an appointment reaches Completed, Cancelled or Failed (if not Rescheduled), a new
appointment must be created if additional work is required.
This lifecycle ensures that appointments follow a controlled process from creation through
execution
while
providing
clear
handling
for
cancellations,
rescheduling,
expiration,
and
execution failures.

Support of polymorphism and extension
patterns
Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by
means
of
a
list
of
generic
meta-attributes
that
we
describe
below.
Polymorphism
in
collections
occurs
when
entities
inherit
from
base
entities,
for
instance
a
PhysicalInterventionAppointment
and
PhoneSupportAppointment
inheriting
properties
from the abstract Appointment entity.
Generic
support
of
polymorphism
and
pattern
extensions
is
described
in
the
TMF
API
Guidelines v3.0 Part 2 document.
The
@type
attribute
provides
a
way
to
represent
the
actual
class
type
of
an
entity.
For
example,
within
a
list
of
Appointment
instances
some
may
be
instances
of
PhysicalInterventionAppointment
where
other
could
be
instances
of
PhoneSupportAppointment.
The
@type
gives
this
information.
All
resources
and
sub-
resources of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.
The
@referredType
can
be
used
within
reference
entities
(like
for
instance
an
AppointmentRef
object)
to
explicitly
denote
the
actual
entity
type
of
the
referred
class.
Notice
that
in
reference
entities
the
@type,
when
used,
denotes
the
class
type
of
the
reference
itself,
such
as
PhysicalInterventionAppointment
or
PhoneSupportAppointment,
and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely
sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.
The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined
properties of an Entity or to specify the expected
characteristics
of an entity.
The
@baseType
attribute
gives
a
way
to
provide
explicitly
the
base
of
class
of
a
given
resource that has been extended.

Attachment sub-resource fields
Complements
the
description
of
an
element
(for
instance
a
product)
through
video,
pictures...
attachmentType
A String [1]. A business characterization of the purpose of
the attachment, for example logo, instructionManual,
contractCopy.
content
A Base64. The actual contents of the attachment object,
embedded inline and encoded as base64. Mutually
exclusive with url.
description
A String. A narrative text describing the content of the
attachment.
href
A String. Hyperlink reference.
id
A String. Unique identifier.
mimeType
A String [1]. A technical characterization of the attachment
content format using an IETF Media Type, for example
application/pdf or image/png. Note: this property is
named mimeType for historical reasons.
name
A String. The name of the attachment.
Appointment User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 9
size
A Quantity. An amount in a given unit.
url
A String. The URL pointing to the attachment content held
in an external system, such as a content management
system or document repository. Mutually exclusive with
content.
validFor
A TimePeriod. A period of time, either as a deadline
(endDateTime only) a startDateTime only, or both.

from

commerce

handling
system.
The

the
system
itself,
the
nature
of

entity
within

(e.g.
class
name)
and
the
unique
ID
of
the
entity
within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for a single entity,
e.g. if the entity passed through multiple systems on the way to the current system. In this
case
the
consumer
is
expected
to
sequence
the
IDs
in
the
array
in
reverse
order
of
provenance, i.e. most recent system first in the list.

API NOTIFICATIONS
For
every
single
of
operation
on
the
entities
use
the
following
templates
and
provide
sample REST notification POST calls.
It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in
the REST Guidelines reproduced below.
Register listener
POST /hub
Description
Sets
the
communication
endpoint
address
the
service
instance
must
use
to
deliver
information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST
calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case
DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.
Request
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
 
"callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
Response
201
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42

Unregister listener
DELETE /hub/{id}
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.
Request
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
Response
204
Publish Event to listener
POST /client/listener
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.
Provides
to
a
registered
listener
the
description
of
the
event
that
was
raised.
The
/client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.
